stack.name: Full Stack Web Developer
stack.summary: A 12-week interview plan for web developers who want depth beyond framework syntax: browser rendering and networking, JavaScript and TypeScript semantics, React internals, backend APIs and SQL, security, testing, distributed systems, deployment and production diagnosis. React, Node.js and PostgreSQL provide concrete examples while the core concepts remain broadly applicable.

materials.title: RenderingNG architecture
materials.subject: Chromium separates style, layout, paint, raster and compositing; eligible visual effects can skip earlier pipeline stages.

materials.title: Inside look at modern web browser (part 2)
materials.subject: Navigation uses network requests, may follow redirects, checks response type and commits the document to a renderer.

materials.title: HTML Standard: scripting
materials.subject: Classic script execution depends on async and defer; module scripts are deferred by default and async changes their scheduling.

materials.title: UI Events
materials.subject: UI events have capture, target and bubble phases; canceling a cancelable event prevents its default action, distinct from stopping propagation.

materials.title: HTML Standard: form control infrastructure
materials.subject: Form submission constructs entries from successful controls; disabled and unchecked controls are omitted and validation can be bypassed by specified APIs or attributes.

materials.title: HTML Standard: input
materials.subject: Input types provide specific constraints; readonly and disabled have different semantics, and checked controls participate in form data.

materials.title: Developing a Keyboard Interface
materials.subject: ARIA does not implement keyboard behavior; composite widgets manage internal focus while Tab moves between components, and focus remains visible.

materials.title: Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions
materials.subject: Controls need accessible names; native labels and visible text are preferred and descriptions provide additional context rather than replacing names.

materials.title: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5
materials.subject: The cascade considers origin, importance and layers before specificity, and inheritance supplies inherited values when applicable.

materials.title: CSS Flexible Box Layout Module Level 1
materials.subject: Flex layout distributes space along a main axis, has automatic minimum sizes, and visual reordering does not change logical navigation order.

materials.title: CSS Grid Layout Module Level 1
materials.subject: Grid defines rows and columns, explicit and implicit tracks, fractional free-space distribution and auto-placement.

materials.title: RFC 9112: HTTP/1.1
materials.subject: HTTP/1.1 permits persistent connections and pipelining but pipelined responses are sent in request order; connection limits are implementation choices.

materials.title: RFC 9113: HTTP/2
materials.subject: HTTP/2 multiplexes streams over a TCP connection, compresses fields, applies flow control and negotiates limits on concurrent streams.

materials.title: RFC 9114: HTTP/3
materials.subject: HTTP/3 maps HTTP onto QUIC streams with independent delivery and transport stream limits; it does not eliminate congestion or application dependencies.

materials.title: RFC 9111: HTTP Caching
materials.subject: HTTP caching distinguishes storage, freshness and validation; no-cache requires validation, no-store prohibits storage, and Vary affects reuse.

materials.title: Fetch Standard
materials.subject: Fetch defines CORS checks, preflights, credentials modes, opaque responses, response status and body consumption.

materials.title: RFC 6265: HTTP State Management Mechanism
materials.subject: Cookie scope uses domain and path; Secure restricts secure transport, HttpOnly restricts script APIs, and expiration uses Max-Age or Expires.

materials.title: ECMAScript: Statements and Declarations
materials.subject: Lexical declarations create block bindings; const prohibits reassignment, and for loops can create per-iteration environments.

materials.title: ECMAScript: Functions and Classes
materials.subject: Functions retain lexical environments; arrow functions use lexical this, and class private fields require their declaring brand.

materials.title: ECMAScript: Ordinary and Exotic Objects
materials.subject: Ordinary property reads follow the prototype chain and getters; writes normally create or update own properties subject to descriptors.

materials.title: HTML Standard: event loops
materials.subject: Browser event loops run tasks and microtask checkpoints; rendering opportunities are scheduled separately and tasks run to completion.

materials.title: ECMAScript: Control Abstraction Objects
materials.subject: Promise executors run during construction, reactions are jobs, chaining propagates results and Promise.all preserves input ordering.

materials.title: ECMAScript: Keyed Collections
materials.subject: Map preserves insertion order and uses SameValueZero equality; weak collections do not keep keys alive or expose key enumeration.

materials.title: ECMAScript: Indexed Collections
materials.subject: Array methods have defined mutation and comparison semantics; sorting without a comparator uses string ordering and copies can be shallow.

materials.title: TypeScript: Narrowing
materials.subject: TypeScript narrows unions through control flow, discriminants and predicates; never supports exhaustive checks.

materials.title: TypeScript: Everyday Types
materials.subject: Type assertions are erased and perform no runtime checks; any disables checks while union members require narrowing.

materials.title: TypeScript: Object Types
materials.subject: TypeScript object types are structural; readonly is a type-checking restriction and excess property checks apply to fresh literals.

materials.title: TypeScript: Generics
materials.subject: Generics preserve relationships between input and output types, and constraints restrict supported operations without discarding the type parameter.

materials.title: TypeScript: Modules - Theory
materials.subject: Module behavior is determined by the runtime host; TypeScript module resolution models the host and type-only imports are erased.

materials.title: TypeScript: Modules
materials.subject: Files with top-level imports or exports are modules with their own scope; dynamic import is asynchronous and type-only imports disappear.

materials.title: Populating the page: how browsers work
materials.subject: DOM, CSSOM and render tree construction followed by layout, paint and compositing.

materials.title: bisect: Array bisection algorithm
materials.subject: Language-independent lower-bound partition invariants and sorted-array insertion cost, implemented in JavaScript.

materials.title: TypeScript: More on Functions
materials.subject: unknown at unvalidated input boundaries and safe typed function signatures.

weeks.title: Browser, HTML and CSS foundations
weeks.goal: Explain navigation, rendering and accessible interaction without relying on a framework.
weeks.deliverable: Build and inspect an accessible responsive form page.
interview_checks: Trace a navigation through network and rendering stages.
Explain event cancellation versus propagation.
Review keyboard behavior and responsive CSS.

lessons.title: Navigation and the rendering pipeline
topics: HTML DOM, CSSOM, render tree, style and layout geometry
lessons.exercise: Record a browser trace for a page, identify a dependent CSS request and compare width and transform animations.

lessons.title: DOM events and semantic form behavior
lessons.exercise: Build a form with delegated interactions; compare preventDefault and propagation stopping, disabled and readonly fields, and checked controls.

lessons.title: Accessibility names and keyboard interaction
lessons.exercise: Audit the page with keyboard and accessibility tree tools; name an icon button and repair a composite widget focus sequence.

lessons.title: CSS cascade and resilient layout
topics: Flex axes and automatic minimum sizes
Grid tracks, placement and logical order
lessons.exercise: Build a card layout with Flex and Grid; explain one cascade conflict and repair a shrinking item without changing DOM reading order.

milestones.title: Build and inspect an accessible responsive form page.

weeks.title: HTTP, caching and browser trust boundaries
weeks.goal: Explain transport concurrency and browser policy without confusing performance limits with protocol guarantees.
weeks.deliverable: Build a cacheable API demo with a deliberate CORS and cookie policy.
interview_checks: Compare HTTP connection and stream concurrency.
Distinguish storage, freshness and validation.
Explain browser credentials and origin checks.

lessons.title: HTTP versions and connection concurrency
lessons.exercise: Inspect negotiated protocols and explain what happens to parallel responses when transport data is lost.

lessons.title: Cache storage, freshness and validators
lessons.exercise: Serve a versioned asset and a personalized endpoint with contrasting cache headers and test revalidation.

lessons.title: Origins, CORS and fetch behavior
topics: Fetch status, opaque responses and bodies
lessons.exercise: Exercise same-origin and cross-origin fetches with and without custom headers and inspect preflight requests.

lessons.title: Cookie scope and session transport
lessons.exercise: Design scoped session cookies and test which requests send them without exposing their values to script.

milestones.title: Build a cacheable API demo with a deliberate CORS and cookie policy.

weeks.title: JavaScript execution and data semantics
weeks.goal: Reason through JavaScript behavior from lexical environments to asynchronous jobs and object identity.
weeks.deliverable: Build a small data widget and explain its asynchronous execution and cleanup.
interview_checks: Trace closures and this binding.
Distinguish tasks from microtasks.
Explain strong and weak collection behavior.

lessons.title: Lexical scope, closures and function binding
topics: Arrow this versus ordinary method calls
lessons.exercise: Trace loop-created callbacks and implement a closure-backed counter without leaking state.

lessons.title: Prototypes, descriptors and object behavior
topics: Class private brands and receiver identity
lessons.exercise: Build a prototype-backed object and explain reads, writes and a private-field receiver failure.

lessons.title: Tasks, microtasks and Promise composition
lessons.exercise: Trace a timer and Promise log order; compose parallel work and handle rejected results deliberately.

lessons.title: Memory, identity and collection contracts
topics: Shallow array copies and shared references
lessons.exercise: Implement an object-keyed cache, compare strong and weak keys and demonstrate a shallow-copy mutation.

milestones.title: Build a small data widget and explain its asynchronous execution and cleanup.

weeks.title: TypeScript boundaries, modules and algorithmic reasoning
weeks.goal: Use types to express contracts while validating runtime input and defending algorithm invariants.
weeks.deliverable: Build a typed module with validated inputs and tested search and deduplication functions.
interview_checks: Explain what TypeScript does not validate at runtime.
Review module host configuration.
Trace binary-search boundary updates and equality choices.

lessons.title: Runtime input and TypeScript narrowing
lessons.exercise: Parse an unknown API payload with explicit validation and handle every variant of a result union.

lessons.title: Structural types and generic relationships
lessons.exercise: Write a generic property reader and review a readonly API for runtime mutability assumptions.

lessons.title: Module hosts and build boundaries
lessons.exercise: Separate type and value imports and explain how a browser bundler or Node host resolves the emitted module.

lessons.title: Arrays, maps and search invariants
lessons.exercise: Implement lower-bound search over sorted numbers and deduplicate primitive and object records with explicit key rules.

milestones.title: Build a typed module with validated inputs and tested search and deduplication functions.

weeks.title: React execution and state
weeks.goal: Trace component execution, queued updates and identity without confusing React work with browser painting.
weeks.deliverable: A tested implementation and a short reasoning note for each lesson exercise.
interview_checks: Explain and defend render, reconciliation and commit using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend state snapshots and update queues using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend component identity and reset behavior using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend hooks and immutable state using a concrete failure scenario.

lessons.title: Render, reconciliation and commit
topics: Pure render calculations and comparison with previous output
lessons.exercise: Trace an update that changes state but leaves JSX identical. Label trigger, render, comparison, commit and browser paint.

lessons.title: State snapshots and update queues
topics: State captured by a render and its event handlers
lessons.exercise: Predict three direct updates, three functional updates, and a mixed replacement/updater sequence; verify with a counter.

lessons.title: Component identity and reset behavior
topics: Stable list keys and sibling identity
lessons.exercise: Build a reorderable editable list with stable IDs, then a keyed recipient form that resets drafts intentionally.

lessons.title: Hooks and immutable state
topics: Custom hooks share logic rather than state
Shallow copying and nested object identity
lessons.exercise: Extract a reusable form hook; repair a conditional hook and a nested-state mutation without adding redundant copies.

milestones.title: Integrate the lesson exercises and review failure scenarios

weeks.title: React synchronization, routes and performance
weeks.goal: Reason about external synchronization, navigation, hydration and measured optimization.
weeks.deliverable: A tested implementation and a short reasoning note for each lesson exercise.
interview_checks: Explain and defend effects, dependencies and request races using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend route matching and data navigation using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend server rendering and hydration using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend measured react optimization using a concrete failure scenario.

lessons.title: Effects, dependencies and request races
topics: Dependencies compare reactive values and capture render snapshots
Cleanup on changes/unmount and stale responses
lessons.exercise: Build a search effect where requests finish out of order; add cleanup and ensure old results cannot replace newer ones.

lessons.title: Route matching and data navigation
topics: Nested route paths and Outlet rendering
Navigation cancellation versus backend request execution
lessons.exercise: Model /projects/:id with an index child and details child; trace overlapping data-router navigations.

lessons.title: Server rendering and hydration
topics: Identical initial server and client output
Effects run on clients and mismatch diagnostics
lessons.exercise: Hydrate a server-rendered page; reproduce a timestamp mismatch, then provide identical initial data and update after hydration.

lessons.title: Measured React optimization
topics: useMemo dependency identity and cached calculations
lessons.exercise: Profile a slow filtered list; compare memoization with stable props against unnecessary memoization and document measured results.

milestones.title: Integrate the lesson exercises and review failure scenarios

weeks.title: Node execution and resilient APIs
weeks.goal: Distinguish event-loop scheduling, worker resources and streaming from safe HTTP boundary design.
weeks.deliverable: A tested implementation and a short reasoning note for each lesson exercise.
interview_checks: Explain and defend event-loop scheduling and latency using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend worker resources and cpu isolation using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend streams and backpressure using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend http api boundaries and error handling using a concrete failure scenario.

lessons.title: Event-loop scheduling and latency
lessons.exercise: Trace timers and callbacks without asserting an unconditional top-level timer/immediate order; measure a CPU loop delaying requests.

lessons.title: Worker resources and CPU isolation
topics: Which asynchronous APIs use the worker pool
Async syntax does not offload arbitrary JavaScript
lessons.exercise: Compare asynchronous filesystem reads with a CPU-heavy JavaScript loop; move CPU work to a reusable worker pool and bound jobs.

lessons.title: Streams and backpressure
lessons.exercise: Stream a large export to a slow writable; respect backpressure and inject a source error to inspect pipeline cleanup.

lessons.title: HTTP API boundaries and error handling
topics: Streaming HTTP bodies and explicit parsing
Untrusted input, parser size limits and validation
Error middleware order and headers already sent
lessons.exercise: Build a bounded JSON endpoint with validation, consistent errors and a streaming response; exercise malformed bodies and failures after headers.

milestones.title: Integrate the lesson exercises and review failure scenarios

weeks.title: Relational correctness and query performance
weeks.goal: Use joins, indexes, transaction isolation and stable pagination to defend data correctness.
weeks.deliverable: A tested implementation and a short reasoning note for each lesson exercise.
interview_checks: Explain and defend joins and database invariants using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend indexes and execution plans using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend transactions and concurrent updates using a concrete failure scenario.
Explain and defend stable pagination under change using a concrete failure scenario.

lessons.title: Joins and database invariants
lessons.exercise: Query customers with and without orders; compare filters in ON and WHERE and enforce order/customer integrity with constraints.

lessons.title: Indexes and execution plans
topics: EXPLAIN estimates versus EXPLAIN ANALYZE actual execution
lessons.exercise: Load a realistic table, compare selective and broad predicates, inspect estimated/actual plans and justify one composite index.

lessons.title: Transactions and concurrent updates
lessons.exercise: Run two sessions updating inventory; compare atomic updates and row locking, then handle a serialization failure by retrying the transaction.

lessons.title: Stable pagination under change
topics: OFFSET skipped-row cost and shifting pages
lessons.exercise: Build offset and keyset pagination ordered by created_at and id; test ties, insertions and a cursor predicate matching the sort.

milestones.title: Integrate the lesson exercises and review failure scenarios

weeks.title: Security boundaries
weeks.goal: Protect identity, resource access and untrusted inputs.
weeks.deliverable: A hardened application with automated authorization and attack-regression tests.
interview_checks: Explain authentication and browser sessions with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain authorization and resource boundaries with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain xss and csrf defenses with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain sql injection and server-side request forgery with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.

lessons.title: Authentication and browser sessions
lessons.exercise: Implement a login session with secure cookie settings, rotation on authentication, expiry and logout; test rejected tokens.

lessons.title: Authorization and resource boundaries
topics: Deny by default and least privilege
lessons.exercise: Test owner, non-owner and administrator access to resource routes, including manipulated identifiers.

lessons.title: XSS and CSRF defenses
topics: HTML sanitization and unsafe DOM sinks
lessons.exercise: Repair an unsafe rendering path and protect a cookie-authenticated write endpoint; demonstrate both defenses with tests.

lessons.title: SQL injection and server-side request forgery
lessons.exercise: Replace unsafe dynamic SQL and constrain a server URL-fetch feature to approved destinations.

milestones.title: A hardened application with automated authorization and attack-regression tests.

weeks.title: Testing and delivery confidence
weeks.goal: Test behavior across unit, component, API and browser boundaries.
weeks.deliverable: A deterministic test suite and CI run with diagnostic artifacts.
interview_checks: Explain unit tests and controlled dependencies with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain component tests and accessible interactions with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain api tests and end-to-end state with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain reliable end-to-end tests and ci with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.

lessons.title: Unit tests and controlled dependencies
lessons.exercise: Test validation and retry logic with injected dependencies, restored spies and controlled time.

lessons.title: Component tests and accessible interactions
lessons.exercise: Test a form by label and role, wait for asynchronous feedback, and assert loading and error states.

lessons.title: API tests and end-to-end state
topics: Seeding and cleanup of test data
lessons.exercise: Create isolated API fixtures, authenticate a browser context, and verify an authorized create-and-read flow.

lessons.title: Reliable end-to-end tests and CI
lessons.exercise: Run a browser flow in CI with traces on first retry; replace fixed sleeps and diagnose one deliberate failure.

milestones.title: A deterministic test suite and CI run with diagnostic artifacts.

weeks.title: System design under failure and scale
weeks.goal: Explain consistency, asynchronous work, retries and transport tradeoffs.
weeks.deliverable: A system design and working queue, cache and retry-safe endpoint.
interview_checks: Explain caching and consistency with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain queues and competing consumers with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain idempotency and transactional event delivery with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain realtime, scaling and resilience with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.

lessons.title: Caching and consistency
topics: Cache expiry and divergent local copies
lessons.exercise: Add cache-aside reads and conditional HTTP responses; test stale-data and cache-control behavior.

lessons.title: Queues and competing consumers
lessons.exercise: Queue background notifications, add an idempotent handler, and isolate repeatedly failing messages.

lessons.title: Idempotency and transactional event delivery
lessons.exercise: Design retry-safe payment creation and an outbox worker, documenting transaction and duplicate-handling boundaries.

lessons.title: Realtime, scaling and resilience

milestones.title: A system design and working queue, cache and retry-safe endpoint.

weeks.title: Production delivery and technical capstone

weeks.deliverable: A containerized deployment, instrumented request flow and measured performance improvement.
interview_checks: Explain containers and production images with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain ci and controlled deployment with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain observability and distributed diagnosis with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.
Explain performance diagnosis and technical capstone with a concrete failure case and tradeoff.

lessons.title: Containers and production images
topics: Build secrets versus persisted image data
lessons.exercise: Build a minimal runtime image with dependency caching, exec-form startup and a secret-mounted build step.

lessons.title: CI and controlled deployment
lessons.exercise: Build a test-and-deploy workflow with constrained permissions, persisted artifacts and a protected environment.

lessons.title: Observability and distributed diagnosis
lessons.exercise: Instrument a request across two services, propagate trace context, and correlate a slow span with structured logs.

lessons.title: Performance diagnosis and technical capstone
topics: Measuring user experience and latency distributions
Node.js event-loop blocking and async work
End-to-end diagnosis from browser to dependency
lessons.exercise: Diagnose a slow authenticated page using browser timings, traces and server evidence; demonstrate fixes and rerun the complete tested deployment.

milestones.title: A containerized deployment, instrumented request flow and measured performance improvement.
